When agents use this

When building menu, popover, tooltip, dialog, toast, disclosure, tab or press feedback.

Skills: jig-mockup.

Browser-free tests cover lifecycle and token contracts. Rendered interpolation, focus and feel remain pending.

Example: A toast closes while it is opening

Before: Restarted keyframes jump back to the first frame.

After / recorded fix: Retarget a transition from the current value and ignore stale close completions.

Why: Rapid input must remain responsive.

Motion recipes

Use these for ordinary components instead of inventing motion per job. Adapted in our own words from animate and its RECIPES.md. The MIT notice covers these adaptations.

Load tokens.css, then recipes.css. Optional recipes.mjs supplies surface lifecycle, tab clipping and FLIP adapters without dependencies. These are motion wrappers for the project's chosen accessible primitives, not a new component library.

General UI stays under 300 ms; explanatory cause-and-effect has a separate 250–1250 ms budget. None of these eight recipes uses that longer budget. Keep explanatory sequences in a separately named motion-ledger entry. Apply the frequency gate first: 100+ uses/day and frequent shortcut/palette navigation settle immediately (instant: true); tens/day usually use stillness or a fade. The person's documented exceptions override source blanket bans.

Surface integration

Put data-motion="menu|popover|tooltip|dialog|toast|backdrop" and data-state="closed" hidden inert on an inner motion wrapper. The primitive's positioner stays outside. For anchored surfaces set --motion-origin from the primitive's collision-aware transform origin, including when it flips sides. An unset origin is an integration defect for menu, popover and tooltip.

import { surfaceMotion } from './motion-lab/recipes.mjs';
const motion = surfaceMotion(wrapper);
// Called by the primitive after it updates its logical open state.
await motion.setOpen(true, { reduced: media.matches, instant: frequent });
// Rapid reversal is allowed; never await a prior open before accepting close.
await motion.setOpen(false, { reduced: media.matches, instant: frequent });

Keep the wrapper mounted until close settles, then let the primitive unmount. Do not add a second exit-presence owner. Focus moves immediately when the logical state changes, never in an animation completion callback. A closing surface is inert immediately; stale completions cannot hide a reopened surface. For a dialog, the primitive retains modal containment/scrim until exit finishes and restores trigger focus safely on dismissal. If the primitive cannot support that lifecycle, dismiss immediately. The motion adapter does not implement focus. Apply the same open target to dialog and backdrop together, without stagger. On hidden tabs, disposal or preference changes call settle(logicalOpen); reapply reduced settings before the next transition. No unseen motion replays.

Accordion / disclosure

Pass stable sibling wrappers to flipLayout(items, changeLayout, options); resolve duration and easing from the CSS tokens with getComputedStyle. Inside changeLayout, update aria-expanded and hidden together. Return focus to the trigger before hiding a focused descendant. For removal, position the leaving object absolutely at its measured location first, then fade it while siblings close the gap concurrently. Remove that exit object on completion or cancellation; never preserve a duplicate in the accessibility tree. The FLIP collapse stage demonstrates removal.

Tabs indicator

The visual duplicate must have aria-hidden="true", inert, no duplicate IDs, and no focusable descendants. Keep its dimensions aligned with the real list. Pass tab bounds relative to the list into tabIndicator(copy, bounds, options). Clipping can paint; profile it under navigation load before using it broadly.

Button press

Add motion-press to the actual button. Keep explicit hover, focus-visible, disabled and active surface styles from the selected theme/primitive. This recipe supplies only the movement; it does not replace those accessible cues.

Evidence and limits

Run node --test tests/motion-recipes.test.mjs for lifecycle races, immediate settling, clipped tab bounds, FLIP reversal and CSS/token contracts for all eight recipes. Run node docs/design-toolbox/motion-lab/check.cjs for stage replay. These are browser-free tests; they do not prove rendered CSS interpolation, native focus/announcement behaviour, paint performance or perceived motion. Before calling a component golden, replay each at normal speed and 2–5× duration, reverse mid-flight, change reduced motion, hide the tab, and inspect it next day.
